oewn-00775967-v.learner: to fight with words; to argue with someone.
examples: The two brothers sparred all evening about who should drive.

oewn-01422848-v.learner: to box with someone using light blows.
examples: He sparred with his trainer for an hour, never hitting hard.

oewn-01422958-v.learner: to fight by striking with spurs, the sharp points on the legs of birds such as roosters.
examples: The two roosters sparred in the yard until the farmer pulled them apart.

oewn-02367699-v.learner: to fit something with spars, the strong poles that hold up a ship's sails.
examples: The workers sparred the new boat before it was sailed for the first time.
Sir William and Lady Lucas were speedily applied to for their consent; and it was bestowed with a most joyful alacrity.
Did she call to refuse her consent?

oewn-00750606-s.learner: hard to deal with, so that you must be very careful and tactful.
examples: if I may mention so delicate a subject
The old map is too delicate to be touched without gloves.

oewn-00709335-a.learner: very fine, subtle, and pleasing, and also easily harmed.
examples: She served the tea in thin, delicate china cups.
A baby's skin is delicate, so keep it out of strong sun.

oewn-01955211-s.learner: worked out with very great fineness and subtlety.
examples: The book draws delicate distinctions between pride and self-respect.

oewn-02111262-s.learner: of a tool or machine: able to measure very small differences or changes exactly.
examples: Only the most delicate scales can weigh a single grain of dust.

oewn-01231281-n.learner: polite and attentive behaviour towards women.
examples: She held out her hand: he kissed it with affectionate gallantry
She was not the better pleased with his gallantry, from the idea it suggested of something more.

connotation.why: chosen over plain 'politeness' to mark attention paid to women

oewn-04864969-n.learner: the qualities of a hero or heroine; very great courage when facing danger, especially in battle.
examples: The soldier was given a medal for gallantry under fire.

oewn-00777876-v.learner: to be against something, or to say that you are against it.
examples: Elizabeth could not oppose such a wish
Elizabeth steadily opposed the scheme.

oewn-02672590-v.learner: to set something against another thing of equal weight or force, so that they balance.
examples: Every push in one direction is opposed by an equal push in the other.

oewn-01093838-v.learner: to fight against something or resist it strongly.
examples: had I been the rector of Longbourn, I should very strenuously have opposed it.

oewn-02383714-v.learner: to act against something, or in opposition to it.
examples: This medicine opposes the effect of the poison.
The older members opposed every change to the rules.

oewn-01083545-v.learner: to set people or things against each other as opponents or rivals.
examples: The final opposed the two best teams in the league.

oewn-00777201-v.learner: to have a disagreement with someone about something.
examples: Do not let us quarrel about the past.
Why could not he keep on quarrelling with you, as his father did before him?

oewn-01634614-v.learner: to set something up again, usually in a better way, or to make something new or like new.
examples: on meeting him accidentally in town, had there renewed a slight acquaintance
The fishing scheme had been renewed the day before

oewn-00167460-v.learner: to make something appear again in a new form.
examples: The old legend was renewed as a modern play.

oewn-08015733-n.learner: either of the two groups, male and female, into which most living things are divided.
examples: Are you so severe upon your own sex as to doubt the possibility of all this?

oewn-00845915-n.learner: the things people do that are connected with sexual intercourse.
examples: They did not have sex until after they were married.

oewn-05014082-n.learner: the features of a living thing that show whether it is male or female, based on its part in producing young.
examples: The doctor could tell the sex of the baby before it was born.

oewn-07502835-n.learner: all the feelings that come from the urge to satisfy sexual desires.
examples: At sixteen his mind was full of sex.

oewn-01126357-s.learner: not famous, and not praised by many people.

oewn-00121594-s.learner: coming from a source that is not known or not named.
